history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV lists the town as 'Koraput', but the shrine is at Gupteswar village on the banks of the Sabari (Kolab) river in Boipariguda block, ~55 km from Jeypore in Koraput district — not in Koraput town. 'Gupteswar' means the Hidden Lord: a limestone cave shrine to Shiva whose gigantic swayambhu linga (reported 2–3 m tall, traditionally believed to be growing in size) sits inside the cave. Legend says Rama discovered the linga during his Dandakaranya exile; it was rediscovered in the 17th century by a tribal hunter and brought to prominence by Maharajah Veer Vikram Dev of Jeypore, who appointed priests. Devotees climb ~200 stone steps through sal and champak forest; a second chamber holds a stalactite revered as the udder of Kamadhenu dripping holy water; in Shravan, Bol Bam pilgrims trek 40–60 km from the Sabari river and over 2 lakh gather for Maha Shivaratri. Local tribes (Bondas, Parajas) revere the site as their guardian deity. COORDINATE FLAG: map geocoder could not resolve the cave site (it matched a Jeypore flour mill and a road listing); coordinates are the Wikipedia-listed Gupteswar Cave values 18.822571, 82.167325 — treat as approximate to the cave area.

name: Gupteswar Temple
town_description: Gupteswar is a forest village in Boipariguda block of Koraput district, on the banks of the Sabari (Kolab) river near the Chhattisgarh border. The cave shrine in the surrounding sal forest draws pilgrims from Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Chhattisgarh.
